ten_test_definitions.V: The real-line full-space Domain: carrier R, nonempty, closed, and convex.
ten_test_definitions.signedA: a_0=-2, a_1=3, a_2=-1, and a_t=4 for every t>=3.
ten_test_definitions.signedW: w_0=0, w_1=-2, and w_t=1 for every t>=2.
ten_test_definitions.eta: eta_1=2 and eta_t=1 for every other natural t, hence globally positive and increasing from index 0 to 1 then decreasing from 1 to 2.
ten_test_definitions.feedback: g_0=1, g_1=-2, and g_t=2 for every t>=2.
ten_test_definitions.realLoss: f_t(z)=<g_t,z>_R=g_t z, a real-valued linear loss on R.
ten_test_definitions.extendedLoss: F_t(z) is the EReal coercion of <g_t,z>_R+0; it is finite everywhere and numerically g_t z.
ten_test_definitions.policy: A SupportPolicy that returns g_t and ignores the supplied previous losses, point history, and current loss. Its value depends only on t.
ten_test_definitions.ogd: The actual iterateVariable output with V, eta, realLoss, and initial point 0; it is not a free sequence with an assumed recurrence.
ten_test_definitions.osd: The actual policy-driven output with V, eta, extendedLoss, initial point 0, and policy; it is not a free sequence with an assumed recurrence.

seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescent.Domain: A carrier set in a real inner-product space, together with proofs of nonemptiness, closedness, and convexity.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescent.project: Classical.choose applied to exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_convex with the domain proofs and z. This expresses the chosen metric-projection point. The underlying Mathlib theorem statement and choice specification are not reproduced in the supplied input.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescent.RegularLoss: There exists an open U containing the carrier such that f is convex on U and differentiable on U. This definition is supplied but is not the FeasibleRegularLoss predicate asserted by the OGD canary.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescent.step: project V (x-eta*gradient f x), with scalar action in the general space. It uses the actual gradient operator.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescent.iterateVariable: At time 0 return the supplied initial point; at time t+1 apply step with eta_t and loss_t to the recursively constructed time-t iterate.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineGradientDescentSource.FeasibleRegu: Convexity of f on the carrier AND differentiability at every carrier point in the ambient real space. No open-neighborhood witness is explicitly required by this predicate.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineConvex.SourceProper: f never equals negative infinity anywhere, and f has at least one finite real value. Positive infinity at other points is not excluded by this predicate alone.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineConvex.SourceSubdifferential: At x, all g such that for EVERY ambient point y, f(x)+<g,y-x> (with the inner product coerced to EReal) <= f(y). This is a global affine-support condition, not only a condition over the carrier.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientDescent.Domain: Alias of OnlineGradientDescent.Domain in the finite-dimensional real-inner-product context.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientDescent.Subdifferentiab: SourceProper f AND nonemptiness of SourceSubdifferential f x at every x in the carrier.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.Domain: Alias of OnlineGradientDescent.Domain in the finite-dimensional real-inner-product context.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.SupportPolicy: At t, accepts the t previous full loss functions indexed by Fin t, the t+1 points indexed by Fin(t+1), and the current full loss function, then returns one vector. Future losses are absent from these arguments; current-loss access is present. This signature does not impose measurability or an oracle-information restriction beyond those arguments.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.history: Constructs the whole point prefix recursively. At t=0 the only point is the supplied initial point. From prefix h through time t, append project V (h[last]-eta_t*p(t, previous losses, h, current loss)).
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.output: The last point of the recursively constructed history at time t.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.selected: The policy value at t supplied with losses at indices <t, history through time t, and loss_t.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineSubgradientPolicy.LegalFeedback: For every t<T, the selected vector is in the global SourceSubdifferential of loss_t at the output at t. This is legality along the actual generated trajectory, not for every possible history.
seventeen_imported_definitions.OnlineHuber.fullSpace: The Domain with carrier Set.univ and its nonempty, closed, convex proofs.

actual_algorithm_assessment: Both algorithm canaries assert values of concrete recursively defined algorithms. OGD uses iterateVariable, step, gradient, and project. OSD uses history, output, selected, and SupportPolicy, with global-subgradient legality asserted separately. Neither theorem has an assumed update recurrence as a hypothesis. With full-space projection interpreted as identity and the linear-loss gradient g_t, the three updates give 0-1*1=-1, -1-2*(-2)=3, and 3-1*2=1. These calculations check the intended mathematical interpretation, not elaboration or proofs of projection/gradient facts.
legality_arithmetic: For the real/extended linear losses, g_t z is finite for every z and g_t x+g_t(y-x)=g_t y for all x,y. Thus the intended support inequality holds with equality; the linear real losses are convex and differentiable with derivative/gradient g_t. This explains the regularity and legality conjuncts mathematically without asserting that their Lean proofs exist.
